sections.h2: Who collects property tax in Brick, New Jersey?
sections.html:
The Brick Township Tax Collector does, from the municipal building at 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723. The office is open weekdays from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. A single bill covers municipal government, public school, county government, library, open space and fire district taxes. Failure to receive a bill does not excuse payment or the interest on late payments.

Brick lies in Ocean County on the Jersey Shore, so assessment appeals go to the Ocean County Board of Taxation, which the township lists at 732-929-2008. The township itself says all appeal questions belong with that board, not with the collector.

sections.h2: When are Brick property taxes due?
sections.html:
Brick bills on a calendar year in four quarters, and each payment is due on the first of the month shown below. The township notes a 10 day grace period, and interest applies to payments received after it.

Brick Township quarterly tax installments
QuarterDue dateMonths it covers
FirstFebruary 1January, February, March
SecondMay 1April, May, June
ThirdAugust 1July, August, September
FourthNovember 1October, November, December

Source: Brick Township Tax Collector.

A seller who missed any of these dates should ask the collector for the balance with interest before closing a sale.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Brick tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in person by check, cash or credit card, send a check by mail, pay online through Paymentus, or sign up for automatic withdrawal. The choice affects whether your money arrives inside the grace period.

  • Online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience fee, and they are not received until the next business day.
  • E-checks are held 10 business days under bank network rules, which can push a payment past the grace period and trigger interest.
  • Automatic withdrawal needs a short form and a voided check, costs nothing and draws during the grace period. You can cancel in writing before a due date.
  • Never mail credit card details. The township does not take online payments for tax sale items or lien redemptions.

Redeeming a tax lien takes a written request at least 72 hours ahead that gives the block, lot and lien number and the date the office will receive payment. Payment must be certified funds, cash or a money order.

sections.h2: What do Brick homes cost, and who owns them?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 gives a median owner occupied home value of $410,600 and median household income of $106,130. Owners live in 82.2 percent of homes. The 2025 population estimate is 77,402, up 5.1 percent from the 73,654 base counted in 2020.

  • Households: 30,289, averaging 2.47 people.
  • Residents 65 and older: 21.4 percent.
  • Median gross rent: $1,756.
  • Monthly owner costs: $2,310 with a mortgage and $949 without.
  • Mean commute: 28.2 minutes.

The township covers 32.22 square miles, of which 20.5 percent is water. Most of it is mainland, but Brick's ocean beach sections sit on the Barnegat Peninsula and are not connected to the rest of the town. It was incorporated on February 15, 1850, and named for Joseph W. Brick of the Bergen Iron Works. The Garden State Parkway opened through it in 1954, followed by a building boom that created neighborhoods such as Lake Riviera, Laurelton and Baywood.

sections.h2: What do added assessments mean for a Brick owner?
sections.html:
New construction creates an extra bill. After work is finished, Brick adds an assessment for the improvement and issues an Added Assessment Bill in October. That bill is due November 1, which is the fourth quarter, and again on February 1 and May 1 of the next year. The collector says it must be paid together with the original bill received in June or July.

The township's building office also warns that work done without permits tends to come up at sale. A buyer's home inspector will ask for proof that additions were approved, and state law allows a penalty of up to $2,000 plus $2,000 for each week the violation continues. Sales are sometimes lost or reduced when unpermitted work is found. If you finished a basement, deck or addition, collect the permits and final approvals before you list.

sections.h2: What should a Brick seller handle besides taxes?
sections.html:
Brick does not require a certificate of occupancy for the resale of a home. A seller must still call the Bureau of Fire Safety at 732-458-4100 for the smoke detector, carbon monoxide detector and fire extinguisher compliance certificate. A leak free oil tank that is still in use may stay in place, and any removal is a negotiation between you and the buyer.

  • Rental houses need a certificate each time a new tenant moves in, and a landlord registers through the Township Clerk with a $100 application fee.
  • Grass and weeds must stay under 10 inches.
  • Unregistered vehicles may not be parked on a residential lot unless they are in a garage.
  • Owners maintain the sidewalk and strip up to the curb, including snow removal.

Brick sits close to Barnegat Bay and the ocean, and the township's building office points owners to FEMA's flood lookup while warning that only a licensed surveyor can confirm a flood zone. Its design criteria list a 115 mph wind load and a 30 inch frost depth. Average annual precipitation in the township is about 46 inches, with nor'easter snow in February.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads serve Brick Township?
sections.html:
Brick Public Schools run 12 schools for pre-kindergarten through grade 12, with 8,414 students enrolled in 2020 to 2021. Two high schools, Brick Memorial and Brick Township, serve grades 9 to 12. Lake Riviera and Veterans Memorial are the middle schools. St. Dominic Elementary and St. Paul's Christian School are private options.

The Garden State Parkway crosses the western part of town with exits 89, 90 and 91, and routes 35, 70 and 88 run through it. Township crews maintain about 256 of the 319 road miles. The Parkway exit at Herbertsville sits near the Monmouth County line, away from the rest of the township.

sections.h2: Is there a tax break for older Brick homeowners?
sections.html: New Jersey offers a $250 deduction to owners who are 65 or older or disabled, have lived in the state a year and own and occupy the home on October 1 of the pretax year. File Form PTD with the assessor or collector, then Form PD5 with the collector by March 1 each year to keep it. A denied claim can be appealed to the county board on Form A-1 by April 1. The township's collector page also points owners to the Division of Taxation for other relief programs.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Brick property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Brick Township Tax Collector at 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723, in person on weekdays from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., by mail, or online through Paymentus. Online card payments carry a 2.5 percent fee.

faqs.q: Who handles a Brick property tax appeal?
faqs.a: The Ocean County Board of Taxation does. The township lists its number as 732-929-2008. State rules set the filing date at April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation or reassessment.

faqs.q: Does Brick give a grace period on tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes, a 10 day grace period follows each due date. Interest applies to payments received after it, and e-checks can arrive late because of a 10 business day processing hold.

faqs.q: Does Brick require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?
faqs.a: No. The township does not require one for resale. You must still get the Bureau of Fire Safety compliance certificate for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher by calling 732-458-4100.

faqs.q: What is an Added Assessment Bill in Brick?
faqs.a: It is a bill for new construction, issued in October after the work is complete. It is due November 1, then February 1 and May 1 of the next year, and it is combined with the regular bill when the following June bills are generated.
